q: A resistor is an electrical device which is used to control the electric current flowing in a circuit.
e: True. A resistor is an electrical device which is used to control the electric current flowing in a circuit. Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift.

q: There are two types of resistors: fixed resistors and variable resistors.
e: True. There are two types of resistors: fixed resistors and variable resistors. There has to stay in that role in the sentence.

q: A rheostat is an example of a fixed resistor.
e: False. A rheostat is a variable resistor used to change the potential difference.

q: If the potential difference across a variable resistor is kept constant, increasing its resistance value will decrease the electric current passing through it.
e: True. If the potential difference across a variable resistor is kept constant, increasing its resistance value will decrease the electric current passing through it. Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage.
